findings.issue_text: [BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...) with no login requirement, so an anonymous GET of /t/:id/unsubscribe raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a redirect to login. Any unauthenticated visitor hitting the new public GET route (it is skip_before_filter :check_xhr and the diff adds no requires_login/requires_user before_filter) crashes with a 500 on current_user.id; email-unsubscribe links opened in a browser without an active session (cookie expired, different device) fail instead of unsubscribing.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls tu.notification_level on a TopicUser that find_by can return nil, raising NoMethodError with a 500 for any logged-in user who has no topic_users row for the topic. A user who follows an unsubscribe link for a topic they never explicitly interacted with (e.g., a notification generated without a persisted TopicUser row, or a hand-typed/shared URL) gets a 500; the obvious edge case of 'user has no record for this topic' is unhandled — the action should default to creating/muting, not assuming the row exists.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action mutates user state on a plain GET with no token and no confirmation, so email-client link prefetchers (Outlook SafeLinks, webmail scanners) will execute the state change without the user ever clicking. Mail providers that prefetch all links in an email hit /t/:id/unsubscribe on delivery and silently flip the user's notification level for the topic before the user reads the email; because the action also toggles (regular->muted, watching->regular), a prefetch plus one real click produces two state changes the user never requested. State-changing GETs on a user-facing email link is a correctness gap the diff never addresses.

[BUG] The action sets tracking/watching topics down to :regular rather than :muted, so the promised 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' is not fulfilled — regular-level topics still email the user for replies, mentions and quotes. A user clicking the new per-topic unsubscribe link in an email keeps receiving notification emails for that topic (any direct reply to their posts), contradicting both the server.en.yml copy ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic') and the client copy ('You will stop receiving notifications'); the requirement the feature is named for is silently dropped for the most common case (watching/tracking).

[BUG] The new %{unsubscribe_url} placeholder in the unsubscribe_link i18n string is not in MessageBuilder's default template_args, so every Email::MessageBuilder consumer with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not pass unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the footer is rendered. Any email path besides send_notification_email that uses add_unsubscribe_link: true (the diff only patched one call site in user_notifications.rb) crashes mail generation with I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, breaking whole email classes; the spec edit in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb (adding unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to message_with_unsubscribe just to keep the existing header test passing) is direct evidence that the builder's default template_args are now insufficient.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser row directly via tu.notification_level= / tu.save!, bypassing TopicUser.change and its bookkeeping (MessageBus publish of notification_level_change, notification_level_changed_at). A user with the topic open in another tab keeps seeing the old notification button state (TopicUser.change publishes a MessageBus message on level change; a direct save does not), and any logic keyed on notification_level_changed_at behaves as if the level never changed — the same mutation done elsewhere in the codebase goes through TopicUser.change for exactly these reasons.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled 'stopNotificiationsText' (Notificiations) and the template at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 must reference the misspelled name to work. Anyone grepping for 'stopNotifications' or 'notifications' to find or extend this binding finds nothing and either duplicates the property or edits the wrong name, silently blanking the page text; the typo is now load-bearing in two places that must stay in sync.

[ADVISORY] The only test touched in this diff asserts the List-Unsubscribe header is present; there is no verification for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe behavior (anonymous access, nil TopicUser, the watching->regular vs regular->muted transitions, the slug-mismatch 301) and no assertion that the unsubscribe_url actually appears in the rendered email body/link. The four behaviors above — the entire server-side feature plus the placement of the new link in the email body — shipped unverified; a regression in any of them (including the two 500s and the copy/behavior mismatch) would pass this suite, which is why they reached the diff in this state.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action dereferences current_user.id with no nil guard, so an anonymous visitor hitting GET /t/:id/unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a login redirect. A user who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email in a browser/device where they are not logged into Discourse (the common email-link case) gets a 500 error page; the app never redirects them to sign in, so the advertised unsubscribe flow fails for logged-out sessions.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by can return nil (a notified user who has never opened the topic has no topic_users row), and the code calls tu.notification_level unguarded, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. A recipient of a mention/reply notification email who never visited the topic clicks the new unsubscribe link and gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed; no TopicUser row is ever created for them either.

[BUG] The unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes it (user_notifications.rb:295); any other Email::MessageBuilder caller using add_unsubscribe_link: true renders with a missing interpolation and I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument, failing email delivery. Any email path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url (e.g., other notification senders or digest-style mail built through MessageBuilder) raises during message construction, so those emails silently stop being sent once this ships.

[BUG] This entire hunk is a pure style refactor (function keyword to ES6 shorthand, var to const, whitespace) with zero behavioral change and no traceable connection to the per-topic unsubscribe feature. The feature PR carries unrelated churn in a hot route file, inflating review surface and blame noise; any regression introduced here is indistinguishable from feature work and unbisectable to the intent of the change.

[BUG] The diff mixes at least four behavior-neutral reformatting changes into topic_user.rb (scope indentation at 7-12, create_lookup block-to-brace at 58-66, MessageBus.publish and where-hash formatting at 110-117/122-127/191-194/215-218) that are not required by or traceable to the unsubscribe feature. Reviewers of the core notification-level model must diff cosmetic churn to verify no behavior changed, and git blame/ar archaeology on this concurrency-sensitive file now points at an unrelated feature commit.

[BUG] The message_builder.rb changes are pure reformatting (hash/literal indentation, gsub spacing) with no functional delta, unrelated to the per-topic unsubscribe requirement. Diff noise in the email pipeline obscures the one real change in this file's vicinity (the new unsubscribe_url template arg), raising the risk that a real behavioral edit smuggled into the reformat goes unreviewed.

[ADVISORY] The summary routes silently drop the post_number: /\d+/ constraint that existed on both t/:slug/:topic_id/summary and t/:topic_id/summary, an unexplained functional change to routing not traceable to the unsubscribe feature. If the post_number constraint was active against request params, requests that previously failed to match now route differently; at minimum, unrelated routing semantics changed inside a feature PR with no commit message or test justifying it.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe endpoint performs a state-mutating action (mutes the user) on a plain GET with no token, so any prefetching agent that fetches links from the email mutates the user's notification level. Email security scanners (e.g., SafeLinks-style prefetchers) and link crawlers that GET the unsubscribe URL will silently mute the user's topic notifications without the user ever clicking; because the operation is a toggle-shaped GET, the user discovers lost notifications with no error to debug.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe controller action has no test anywhere in this diff, despite containing non-trivial branching (slug mismatch redirect, JSON-vs-HTML format check, notification-level toggle). Any regression in the toggle direction, the slug redirect, or the nil-handling paths above ships undetected; the failure mode is silently muted (or unmuted) users, which no other spec exercises.

[ADVISORY] The action mutates TopicUser directly via tu.notification_level= and tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change, bypassing the MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change publish and the notification_level_reason bookkeeping that TopicUser.change maintains. A user with the topic open in another tab keeps a stale notification-level UI (no live update), and the persisted notification_level_reason no longer explains why the level changed, degrading the audit/debug path used elsewhere.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled stopNotificiationsText ('Notificiations') and the template must spell it identically for the page to render. The next developer who 'fixes' the spelling in only one of the two places breaks the unsubscribe page's headline; the misspelled identifier also defeats text search for 'notification' across the codebase.

[BUG] topics_controller#unsubscribe calls tu.notification_level on the result of TopicUser.find_by without a nil check, so a user with no topic_users row for the topic crashes with NoMethodError and gets a 500 instead of the unsubscribe behavior. Any logged-in user who opens the per-topic unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row exists (e.g. a link from an old email, a row purged, or a user clicking the URL for a topic they never touched) hits `tu.notification_level` on nil -> NoMethodError -> 500 page; the intended mute/regular transition never happens.

[BUG] The comparison `tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` crashes with NoMethodError when notification_level is NULL, a state this very diff's topic_user.rb tracking scope explicitly expects via COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular). A topic_users row created without a notification_level (the COALESCE guard in the tracking scope in this diff is the codebase's own admission such rows exist) makes the nil > integer comparison raise NoMethodError -> 500 for the user clicking the email unsubscribe link, so the feature silently fails for exactly the rows the scope defends against.

[BUG] The unsubscribe_link i18n string in config/locales/server.en.yml now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but Email::MessageBuilder supplies no default for it and only send_notification_email was taught to pass it, so any other caller using add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g. digest-style emails built through the same MessageBuilder path) renders the footer with I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument. Every email path that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url raises while building the html/text part, so those emails fail to render and are not delivered; the failure is invisible until the first non-notification email is sent after deploy.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe action creates a parallel write path to TopicUser by doing a raw find + attribute assignment + save! instead of going through TopicUser.change, bypassing the MessageBus notification_level_change publish and the bookkeeping TopicUser.change performs. Other live browser sessions of the same user never receive the /topic/:id notification_level_change message, so their notification dropdown keeps showing the old state until reload; and any future bookkeeping added to TopicUser.change (e.g. notification_level_changed_at) silently does not apply to unsubscribe-driven changes, which is the divergence the TopicUser.change API exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] The template now renders %{respond_instructions} unconditionally at the bottom while keeping the original occurrence inside the context_posts block, so emails with context posts print the respond/instructions footer twice. Recipients of notification emails that include context posts see a duplicated 'to respond, visit...' footer block in every such email, which looks like a rendering mistake rather than intentional layout.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe action's behavior-bearing logic (slug-mismatch redirect, the notification-level toggle, nil-row handling, save!) ships with no test in this diff; the only test added covers the List-Unsubscribe header in message_builder_spec. A regression in the toggle condition (e.g. swapping regular/muted) or in the nil-row path would go green in CI and ship, silently munging users' per-topic notification levels via the emailed link with no test failure to catch it.

[BUG] The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires an %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation, but only send_notification_email was updated to pass it, so every other mailer that uses add_unsubscribe_link: true raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when MessageBuilder#html_part calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) without that key. All notification emails other than post-notification emails fail to render their body (email delivery raises), silently breaking the existing per-topic-unrelated unsubscribe footer that review iterations converted from an always-satisfiable template into one with a new required argument without updating all call sites. The diff's own spec change is the smoking gun: message_with_unsubscribe had to gain unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to keep passing.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action calls current_user.id, but for an anonymous visitor this is nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a redirect to login. A user who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link in an email from a browser where they are not logged in (the most common case for emailed links) gets a 500 error page; the skip_before_filter :check_xhr change explicitly makes this non-XHR, unauthenticated GET path reachable, and topics#show's public access means no login gate protects it.

[BUG] TopicUser.find_by returns nil for users with no TopicUser record for this topic, and tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError, returning a 500. Any user who received the notification email without a pre-existing topic_users row (e.g., the record was never created for their notification path) clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link and gets a server error instead of having their notification level set; the action performs no nil check and no TopicUser.create fallback, unlike every other notification-level mutation which goes through TopicUser.change.

[BUG] The action implements a toggle (watching/tracking demotes only to :regular, otherwise mutes), which contradicts both the feature intent ('per-topic unsubscribe') and the page copy 'You will stop receiving notifications' — a watching user clicking the link is demoted to regular and still receives reply/mention notifications, and clicking the same emailed link a second time re-enables notifications. Users who follow the email's unsubscribe link while watching a topic keep getting notified while the UI tells them notifications stopped; and because the GET endpoint is a toggle, re-opening or re-clicking the same email link (e.g., from mail preview caching or a second device) silently re-subscribes them, the opposite of the accepted objective.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe endpoint is an unauthenticated-CSRF-reachable GET that mutates notification state: any embedded in a web page or email fires it with the victim's session cookie and flips their notification level. A third party can silently toggle (mute or re-enable) a logged-in user's per-topic notifications by getting them to load any page containing the image tag; there is no CSRF token or POST requirement on a state-changing endpoint.

[ADVISORY] tu.save! mutates notification_level directly, creating a second hand-maintained code path for notification-level changes that bypasses TopicUser.change (its MessageBus publish of notification_level_change and its normalization/rescue behavior). After unsubscribing via this endpoint, other open sessions/tabs of the same user never receive the MessageBus notification_level_change message that every other level change emits, so their UI shows stale notification state; the next change to TopicUser.change's invariants (or to this copy) silently diverges the two paths.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i'), and the template in topic/unsubscribe.hbs must reference the same misspelling for the page to work. The misspelling is now load-bearing across two files; anyone who 'fixes' the name in one file (grep for the obvious spelling finds nothing, or fixes only one occurrence) breaks the unsubscribe page's primary text with no error pointing at the cause.

[ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff covers MessageBuilder's unsubscribe_url plumbing; the new unsubscribe controller action — including the nil TopicUser crash, the anonymous-user crash, the toggle semantics, and the slug-mismatch redirect — has no spec anywhere in the diff. A regression in the toggle or redirect logic (or the two nil crashes above) ships silently; the behavior-bearing new endpoint is exactly the code most likely to be refactored next given the surrounding formatting churn in this file, with nothing to catch it.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action mutates the user's notification_level in response to a plain GET request routed via `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`, so the write is CSRF-protected by nothing (Rails forgery protection ignores GETs and the XHR check is skipped). An attacker embeds `` (or a link-prefetching client hits the email link) and forces a logged-in victim's notification level on any topic id down to regular/muted without consent; two img hits force a watching topic fully to muted, silently suppressing the victim's notifications.

[BUG] For a logged-in user who has no TopicUser row for the topic (never visited, or the row was purged), `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a graceful handling path. Any logged-in user visiting /t/<visible_topic_id>/unsubscribe for a topic they have no TopicUser record for gets a 500 error page; the new unsubscribe URL advertised in every notification email becomes a crash vector for exactly this state.

[ADVISORY] The `unsubscribe_link` i18n string now requires an `unsubscribe_url` template argument, but only send_notification_email in this diff was updated to pass it; any other Email::MessageBuilder call site that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will hit `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with a missing interpolation argument. I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument is raised during email construction for those senders, so the affected notification/digest emails stop being delivered (the sending job fails) rather than degrading to the old preferences-only link; the spec at spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb had to add unsubscribe_url to the existing test precisely because the contract changed for all callers.

[BUG] The spec fixture now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` but no assertion in the spec verifies that this URL reaches the List-Unsubscribe header or the rendered unsubscribe_link body — the only changed/visible assertion remains `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present`, which passes regardless of whether the per-topic URL is used, is correct, or even absolute. A regression that drops unsubscribe_url from the header_args or from the I18n template_args (leaving emails with only the generic preferences link) would pass this suite, giving false confidence that the feature in this diff is covered.

[BUG] The new `unsubscribe` action dereferences `current_user.id` and `tu.notification_level` (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` then `tu.notification_level`) with no nil guard, so it raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 when the email link is opened by an anonymous visitor (current_user is nil, since only check_xhr was skipped) or when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic (TopicUser.find_by returns nil). A user clicking the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email client that prefetches/fetches without the session cookie, or a user who received the email but never opened the topic (no TopicUser record exists yet), gets a 500 error instead of an unsubscribe page — the feature's core flow is broken for exactly the cases it targets.

[BUG] The `unsubscribe_link` translation now unconditionally interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `Email::MessageBuilder` renders it via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every message built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, and only `send_notification_email` was taught to pass `unsubscribe_url` — any other builder caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at email build time. Any email path in this codebase (present or added later) that opts into the unsubscribe link without also passing the new option crashes when generating the email body; the spec change added `unsubscribe_url` to the fixture precisely to dodge this, masking the missing-argument contract rather than testing it.

[ADVISORY] The new client-side route, controller (controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), and template (templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs) ship with no JavaScript spec exercising the model load, the afterModel nulling of notificationReasonText, or the template rendering `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`. A regression in the route's model hook or in the typo'd computed property (which the template references via triple-stache unescaped) ships silently; the only changed test file in this diff (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb) covers none of the client behavior, so a broken unsubscribe page would only be discovered manually.

[ADVISORY] The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` (three i's, 'Notificiations') and, because the template references it by the same misspelled name, the misspelling becomes a load-bearing public symbol rather than a fixable typo. Anyone grepping for 'notifications' or 'stop_notifications' to maintain this controller will not find the property, and a well-intentioned rename of the property (fixing the typo) without touching the template's `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders an empty page with no error at the call site.

[BUG] topics_controller#unsubscribe raises NoMethodError (500) when current_user is nil (anonymous visitor) or when TopicUser.find_by returns nil, because it calls current_user.id and tu.notification_level with no nil guard. A user who is not logged in (arriving from the email link in another browser/session, where the link is the primary flow) hits `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` with current_user == nil -> NoMethodError -> 500 instead of a redirect to login. Separately, a logged-in user can have no topic_users row (e.g. the email came from a category watch or a mention, which do not create a per-topic TopicUser), so find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises -> 500 on exactly the click this feature exists to serve. The diff's own topic_user.rb tracking scope uses COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular) (app/models/topic_user.rb line ~10), proving the column is nullable, so even an existing row with a NULL notification_level makes the bare `tu.notification_level > ...` comparison raise -> 500.

[BUG] html_part now calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) against a template that requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url, so every other MessageBuilder caller with add_unsubscribe_link: true raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the email footer is built. Any mailer that opts into add_unsubscribe_link without also passing unsubscribe_url (e.g. the digest mailer in app/mailers/user_notifications.rb, which historically sets add_unsubscribe_link: true and was not touched by this diff) now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument during html_part, crashing email generation for that entire mail type for all users -- a regression introduced by the new two-line unsubscribe_link text in config/locales/server.en.yml that previously only referenced %{user_preferences_url}. The updated spec (spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb line ~170) only exercises the passing-unsubscribe_url path, so the broken path is untested.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET endpoint, so email-client link prefetching (SafeLinks, anti-spam scanners, mail proxies) mutes the topic without the user ever clicking. Mail infrastructure that warms/validates links (Outlook SafeLinks, corporate scanners, feed readers) performs a GET on the unsubscribe URL, silently executing the notification_level change; the user later discovers the topic muted with no indication anything ran, and because the mutation already happened there is no confirmation step to cancel. A POST-with-CSRF-token or a tokenized one-click link pattern would avoid the prefetch side effect.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser row via direct tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change, so it skips the MessageBus.publish('/topic/...', {notification_level_change: ...}) that every other notification-level mutation in the codebase performs. A user with the topic open in another tab or a second device never receives the notification_level_change MessageBus message, so those sessions keep displaying the old notification state indefinitely until a full reload; the operation is only partially propagated while the endpoint responds as if it fully succeeded. Anchored against app/models/topic_user.rb lines 113-115 and 194/218, where TopicUser.change always pairs the level change with a MessageBus publish.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe page unconditionally states "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}", but the controller's toggle logic sets notification_level to :regular (not :muted) whenever the current level is above regular, so the operation does not do what the copy claims. A tracking/watching user clicks the link, is demoted only to :regular, and continues to receive reply/mention notification emails for that topic, while the page asserts notifications have stopped; the mismatch misdirects support debugging ('I unsubscribed but still got an email') and misrepresents the endpoint's behavior to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET endpoint, so email-client link prefetching (SafeLinks, anti-spam scanners, mail proxies) mutes the topic without the user ever clicking. Mail infrastructure that warms/validates links (Outlook SafeLinks, corporate scanners, feed readers) performs a GET on the unsubscribe URL, silently executing the notification_level change; the user later discovers the topic muted with no indication anything ran, and because the mutation already happened there is no confirmation step to cancel. A POST-with-CSRF-token or a tokenized one-click link pattern would avoid the prefetch side effect.

Because this is a state-changing GET endpoint with no confirmation/token/CSRF protection shown, any automated GET (email link scanners/prefetchers) would execute the mute/regular toggle without an explicit user action, matching the finding.
